subject: Private fleet upgrade: risk allocation, pinning windows & rollback agreement
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: John Wu <j.wu@atlasbank.com>, AtlasBank SRE <sre@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private fleet upgrade: risk allocation, pinning windows & rollback agreement

John / Atlas SRE team,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (map_v1.xlsx) and a short rollback checklist stub (rollback_checklist.md). High-level ask: we want to lock down a maintenance window and agree the failure thresholds and rollback authority before we schedule the actual upgrade.

Proposed items for this thread:
- Version pin: we will pin to v2.3.1 for your production rack and stage v2.4.0 in canary for 48 hours.
- Maintenance window: narrow window (Sat 03:00-05:00 UTC) with a 90-minute active cutover.
- Rollback authority: Atlas SRE holds final go/no-go within the active cutover; Redwood ops will nominate Karthik as fallback approver.
- Abort criteria (examples): sustained 5%+ p99 latency regression for >5m, failed health checks >2 nodes in the same shard, or >1% token error increase.

Questions for you: preferred weekend? Are we ok with a snapshot-based rollback (fast restore to pinned image) or do you need live-slice rollback? Also confirm any blackout dates in June.

Next steps: once we align here I’ll update the MAP and send a DocuSign for the schedule change.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: map_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), rollback_checklist.md (text)

Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: risk allocation, pinning windows & rollback agreement

Sean —

Thanks, this is a good start. A couple of notes from our side after quick ops sync: 

- Weekend preference: Saturday is fine, but prefer 02:00-04:00 UTC (shifted one hour earlier) because of downstream batch jobs at 06:00.
- Rollback: Atlas policy prefers live-slice rollback where feasible (we avoid full restore when possible). Can you confirm the expected recovery delta for both approaches?
- KV cache: any KV cache invalidation during rollback will cause cold-start tail latency. Need a clear cache-warm plan.
- SLA/credits: unclear on how a prolonged rollback ( > 2 hours active outage) affects our contract; can you flag escalation channel and preliminary credit calculus?

I’ve attached a short Ops checklist (I’m forwarding it in the thread). If you can address the KV/cache and recovery delta items we can sign off on the window.

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: John Wu <j.wu@atlasbank.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: risk allocation, pinning windows & rollback agreement

John — quick technical notes from SRE/Platform: 

- Recovery delta estimates:
  * Snapshot-based full restore: expected restore-to-traffic time ~18-30 minutes depending on dataset size; cold-KV fill increases p99 for ~20-45m after restore unless we pre-warm.
  * Live-slice rollback (preferred by Atlas): we can support a blue/green style traffic cutover with dual write-mirroring for ~30m before switch; rollback via traffic re-route is ~5-7 minutes to re-establish prior steady-state, with lower long-tail impact.

- KV cache warm plan:
  * Pre-seed with top-10% hot keys using a warmed snapshot (we can run a background rehydrate job during the 48h canary).
  * If rollback triggered, we will replay the last 2 hours of requests from our audit log to rehydrate prioritized cache buckets — plan detailed in rollback_checklist.md.

- Abort metrics (we recommend the following thresholds):
  * p99 latency increase >= 5% sustained for 5 minutes
  * request error rate increase >= 0.8% for 3 minutes
  * any repeated OOMs or GPU memory thrash on >1 node in same availability zone

- Canary plan: stage 5% traffic to v2.4.0 for 2 hours, 25% for 12 hours, then 100% in rolling fashion after a green signal. We will not pin production until we pass regression checks.

I’ve attached the working rollback_checklist.md to this email with the warm/replay steps and the specific Prometheus/trace queries we’ll use as gates. Also created runbook ticket RB-3421 for the preflight dry-run; Monica will lead the dry-run and Karthik will own the live cutover.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: rollback_checklist.md

Subject: Re: Private fleet upgrade: risk allocation, pinning windows & rollback agreement

John —

Thanks for the quick follow-ups. We’re aligned on these points and will proceed with the adjusted window: Saturday 02:00-04:00 UTC. Summary of agreed items below (I’ll update the MAP and send the DocuSign once you confirm):

Agreed: 
- Window: Sat 02:00-04:00 UTC (90-minute active), target date: 2025-06-14 (pending your final blackout check).
- Rollback approach: live-slice blue/green by default; snapshot-restore allowed as last resort.
- Preflight: dry-run RB-3421 led by Monica, scheduled two weeks ahead (Monica will propose dates).
- Abort gates: use Naomi’s recommended metrics; Karthik is final fallback approver if Atlas SRE is unreachable.
- Credits/escalation: Sean (me) will triage contract impacts; I’ve looped Legal/Revenue (not on this thread) to prepare a preliminary credit table for >2 hour outages.

Action items:
- John: confirm blackout dates and approve the 2025-06-14 tentative date.
- Monica: propose dry-run dates and perform preflight with RB-3421.
- Karthik: prepare the emergency rollback runbook and test the rehydration job in staging.

Once John confirms we’ll finalize the MAP (map_v1.xlsx) and send a DocuSign for the schedule change.

Best,
Sean
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
